title: State Tretyakov Gallery: Masterpieces
subtitle: Portraits, invented beings and political allegories test the distance between a person and an emblem.
introduction:
A girl at a table needs peaches, a knife and a light-filled room to make her particular setting clear. Kustodiev's enormous Bolshevik, by contrast, strides above buildings that cannot contain him. The difference is a question of scale and purpose, not simply of accurate and inaccurate bodies. One picture gives a sitter a lived setting; the other makes a body carry a political force.

Between these extremes, the selection includes portraits whose names are known, a woman whose identity remains unresolved, and figures drawn from history or legend. Landscapes complicate the comparison by making people small or dispensing with them. *Black Square* withdraws the recognisable scene altogether, while remaining a physical painted object.
visitNote: The Tretyakov Gallery uses several buildings for different parts of its collection. This selection is not a single-building route, and loans or conservation can interrupt display. Check the location of individual works before travelling. The guide distinguishes painted historical and legendary subjects from eyewitness records.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by Michael Sadleir
books.note: Kandinsky’s book offers a contemporary argument for painting beyond literal representation. Read it beside Black Square as another position within early modern art, not as a statement of Malevich’s own programme or beliefs.

works.title: Girl with Peaches
works.credit: Valentin Serov. Girl with Peaches. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The peaches and knife keep the table available for ordinary use rather than making it a ceremonial portrait prop. Serov's light extends beyond the girl's shoulders, so the room continues around her settled yet loose pose. The image gives an impression of a moment within daily life. That effect is a pictorial achievement, not proof that the painting required only a moment to make.

works.title: Black Square
works.credit: Kazimir Malevich. Black Square. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: No depicted person or landscape provides an entry into the dark quadrilateral. Malevich makes its relationship with the pale field the painting's overt proposition. Yet the edges are not mechanically perfect, and the aged surface has cracks. An apparently absolute form exists here in material with a history. Recognising that fact does not require turning it back into a hidden illustrated scene.

works.title: Seated Demon
works.credit: Mikhail Vrubel. Seated Demon. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The powerful body has little room to extend within the low format. Clasped hands and a hunched posture keep its strength contained, while angular, flower-like forms connect it to the surrounding surface. Vrubel gives an imagined being a conflict of scale: the figure seems capable of force, yet its present arrangement prevents that force from becoming uncomplicated action.

works.title: March
works.credit: Isaac Levitan. March. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Melting snow exposes a track that is neither fully winter ground nor fully cleared earth. Warm light on the wooden building contrasts with blue shadows among the trees. Levitan makes seasonal change visible as simultaneous conditions, not a clean replacement of one season by another. The waiting horse supplies an ordinary pause within that longer transformation.

works.title: Bathing a Red Horse
works.credit: Kuzma Petrov-Vodkin. Bathing of a Red Horse. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The horse's broad red flank dominates figures and water that remain recognisable as a bathing scene. Petrov-Vodkin keeps bodily weight while departing from expected colour and ordinary scale. That combination lets the animal exceed a purely descriptive role without becoming unreadable. Its symbolic possibilities begin in the disproportion the picture makes visible, rather than in one compulsory explanation.

works.title: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan
works.catalogueTitle: Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan on November 16, 1581
works.credit: Ilya Repin. Ivan the Terrible and His Son Ivan on November 16, 1581. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The older man's supporting hands cannot reverse the wound around which the bodies are joined. Repin stages the aftermath of violence, with patterned carpets and rich furnishings continuing around an embrace that has become desperate. The image is a historical reconstruction, not eyewitness evidence. Its strongest argument is made through the failure of a protective gesture to undo what preceded it.

works.title: Portrait of an Unknown Woman
works.credit: Ivan Kramskoi. Portrait of an Unknown Woman. Image credit: Ivan Kramskoi. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The raised carriage seat positions the woman's direct look above the snowy street. Fashionable dark clothing contributes to a carefully presented public appearance. Kramskoi makes the encounter specific while leaving identity unresolved. The temptation to supply a biography from the costume or expression should be resisted: the picture gives a convincing presence, not enough evidence for a name or personal story.

works.title: The Vision of the Young Bartholomew
works.catalogueTitle: The Vision of the Young Bartholomew
works.credit: Mikhail Nesterov. The Vision of the Young Bartholomew. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The boy and hooded monk meet at the edge of a broad, recognisable landscape. Inclined heads and small gestures give the sacred episode a close human scale. Nesterov does not remove the encounter from ordinary fields and woodland. The setting matters because it allows the extraordinary event to inhabit terrain that remains physically comprehensible.

works.title: After Prince Igor's Battle
works.credit: Viktor Vasnetsov. After prince Igor’s battle. Image credit: Viktor Vasnetsov. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The warriors can no longer act within the landscape that contains them. Birds, scattered weapons and shields give the open ground details through which the aftermath becomes readable. Vasnetsov shifts the literary-historical battle from combat to stillness. The absence of an active hero makes the bodies left behind, rather than a climactic individual deed, the substance of the scene.

works.title: Portrait of Modest Mussorgsky
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of the Composer Modest Musorgsky
works.credit: Ilya Repin. Portrait of the Composer Modest Musorgsky. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The loose dressing gown does not supply the formal public costume expected in a portrait of a distinguished composer. Repin keeps untidy hair and reddened features available to inspection. The likeness grants physical frailty the same sustained attention as recognition. It need not translate every sign of condition into a moral judgment or a diagnosis to remain exacting.

works.title: Portrait of Leo Tolstoy
works.credit: Ivan Kramskoi. Portrait of Leo Tolstoy. Image credit: Ivan Kramskoi. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The dark loose shirt and restrained ground offer few accessories through which to identify a celebrated writer. Kramskoi directs attention instead towards the gaze, beard and low-gathered hands. The portrait relies on the particular body's presence rather than a library or literary emblem. Simplicity is still a choice of presentation, not the absence of one.

works.title: A Quiet Monastery
works.credit: Isaac Levitan. Quiet cloister. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The narrow bridge offers a route across reflective water towards the monastery buildings. Levitan makes the distant religious site reachable within the landscape instead of isolating it as an architectural icon. Trees and water separate the stages of approach. The quiet depends on those measured intervals, with a possible human passage remaining present even when no large figure directs it.

works.title: Evening Bells
works.credit: Isaac Levitan. Vesper chimes. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/isaac-levitan/vesper-chimes-1892
works.description: The title introduces a sound the painting cannot literally produce. Broad water and remote monastery buildings supply the imagined distance across which it might travel. Levitan gives that suggestion a physical setting through reflection, boats and evening clouds. The visual account remains precise enough that the named sound adds an association rather than replacing the landscape's structure.

works.title: Overseas Guests
works.credit: Nicholas Roerich. Overseas Guests. Image credit: Nicholas Roerich. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The red sails and repeated shields make the vessel a conspicuous pattern as well as a means of travel. Roerich constructs a distant historical world through strong colour and ornament. Boats and rocky shores preserve the setting, but the ship's surface demands attention in its own right. The result is an imagined past with a visibly designed appearance.

works.title: The Beekeeper
works.credit: Ivan Kramskoi. Beekeeper. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/ivan-kramskoy/beekeeper-1872
works.description: The staff, pale shirt and lowered head define an elderly man among plants and wooden hives. Kramskoi keeps the figure within the conditions of work rather than detaching him as a generalised emblem of the countryside. His slow posture contrasts with the dense growth. The surrounding ground has uses and occupations beyond serving as a background for age.

works.title: Country Road
works.credit: Alexei Savrasov. Country road. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/aleksey-savrasov/country-road-1873
works.description: Ruts and pools make the road an uneven way into the view. Savrasov retains the effects of weather on ground that might otherwise serve as a smooth perspective device. Broken clouds and changing light connect the near surface to the sky. The landscape becomes traversable in a bodily sense, including the difficulties of making that passage.

works.title: The Snow Maiden
works.credit: Viktor Vasnetsov. Snow Maiden. Image credit: Viktor Vasnetsov. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The pale costume separates the girl from a forest that remains dark around her. Vasnetsov gives a legendary figure a particular place of exposure, between illuminated snow and enclosing trees. The contrast is enough to establish a precarious presence without retelling every part of the tale. The setting contributes to her condition rather than merely identifying a season.

works.title: The Bolshevik
works.credit: Boris Kustodiev. The Bolshevik. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The banner carrier is too large for the streets and roofs beneath him. Kustodiev makes political force visible through this deliberate mismatch of scale. The crowded city becomes the ground over which an allegorical body strides. The painting offers a constructed image of revolutionary power; its emphatic figure should not be mistaken for an impartial summary of the events it invokes.

works.title: The Philosophers Bulgakov and Florensky
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of the philosophers S.N. Bulgakov and P.A. Florensky
works.credit: Mikhail Nesterov. Portrait of the philosophers S.N. Bulgakov and P.A. Florensky. Image credit: Mikhail Nesterov. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Walking side by side supplies the paired portrait with an ordinary shared action. Pale and dark clothing distinguish the men before their separate looks and gestures are considered. Nesterov makes intellectual companionship visible without requiring an emblem of abstract thought. Togetherness remains compatible with different states of attention, held within the same path rather than the same expression.

works.title: Ivan Morozov
works.credit: Valentin Serov. Ivan Morozov. Image credit: Unknown author Unknown author. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The sitter's sober clothing stands against pictures whose colours remain markedly more active. Serov gives a collector an identity partly through the art occupying his surroundings. Clasped hands anchor the near figure while the background records chosen visual company. A portrait can therefore describe taste through an arrangement of things without needing to illustrate every detail of a life.

closingSections.title: Keep scale in view
paragraphs: Compare the ordinary-sized portrait sitter with the enlarged allegorical figure, then return to a landscape in which people barely appear. Scale changes what a body can stand for. The Tretyakov's works are distributed across venues and changing displays; check current location information before treating the selection as a visit plan.
